findings.title: BFF transforms text before enforcing the approved byte constraint
findings.rationale: ConversationsController.responder uses String(body.texto).trim() before forwarding text to OutboundService. Consequently, 500 accented characters followed by one space comprise 1001 UTF-8 bytes but become 1000 bytes and can be dispatched instead of rejected. Valid text containing surrounding whitespace is also changed, and non-string payloads can become sendable text through coercion. This conflicts with the human-admitted preservation of valid text and the package's explicit exact-payload requirement. The new native byte case tests only unpadded strings and therefore misses this boundary defect. The shared policy and provider-client checks correctly validate the transformed value, so they cannot recover the original request.
findings.suggested_action: Require texto to be a string, use trim only to determine emptiness, and pass the original string unchanged to the abstract policy validation and sender. Add real BFF regressions proving that whitespace-padded over-limit requests produce zero reservations, claims and provider calls, valid whitespace-containing payloads reach the provider unchanged, and non-string values are rejected.
